page: Amazon Web Services m3.large is a general-purpose, third-generation virtual machine running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.75 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 32 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position the m3.large in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is weak, falling in the bottom 25% with a score of 1301.38, while multi-core performance drops to the bottom 10% at 1706.78. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large block read and write speeds recorded at 14.03 GB/sec and 12.02 GB/sec respectively, both placing in the bottom 10%. Real-world application benchmarks reflect these constraints, showing a static web serving throughput of 1.95 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 0.8 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m3.large represents a legacy hardware profile with low resource density. While it offers dedicated CPU allocation and bundled local NVMe storage, its performance-per-resource ratio is low compared to newer generations. This instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic web serving, development environments, simple text processing, or legacy applications that do not require high computational throughput or modern instruction sets.
